title: AlphaEvolve finds a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices, a rank that Kaporin had reported in 2024, and researchers outside DeepMind derive rational variants from its decomposition
summary: In May 2025 DeepMind reported that its Gemini-powered coding agent AlphaEvolve had found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices, a rank that Igor Kaporin had reported in 2024.
account: In a Doklady Mathematics paper published online on 20 October 2024, Igor Kaporin of the Russian Academy of Sciences reported a 48-multiplication design for 4x4 matrices that he found by numerical search. On 14 May 2025 Google DeepMind announced AlphaEvolve, a Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent. DeepMind reported that it had found an algorithm multiplying two 4x4 complex-valued matrices with 48 scalar multiplications, improving on the 49 obtained from two recursion levels of Strassen's 1969 algorithm. The makers' technical paper, posted on 16 June 2025, states that AlphaEvolve is the first method to find a rank-48 algorithm for these matrices. The AlphaEvolve paper does not cite Kaporin's paper. On 16 June 2025 Jean-Guillaume Dumas, Clément Pernet and Alexandre Sedoglavic (CASC and CRIStAL, France), researchers independent of DeepMind, posted a preprint. It presents a 48-multiplication algorithm with only rational coefficients, removing the need for complex arithmetic. They state that it was derived from AlphaEvolve's algorithm under the action of an isotropy that projects the decomposition onto the field of rational numbers. The derivation is therefore not independent of the AI result. The first version of the preprint contains no explicit verification statement. On 19 March 2026 the same authors posted a more accurate variant of that rational algorithm, valid over any ring containing an inverse of 2. In a peer-reviewed ISSAC 2026 paper of 12 July 2026, Yoav Moran, Oded Schwartz and Shuncheng Yuan recover the rational form of AlphaEvolve's scheme by a general method and prove that the scheme has no integer-coefficient equivalent. On 16 July 2026 Li, Wang and Hu, of Zhejiang University of Technology and the National University of Defense Technology, posted a preprint in which they find infinitely many inequivalent rational 48-multiplication algorithms. Version 7 of the Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic preprint (27 July 2026) embeds a Maple program that checks their rational algorithm. On 10 September 2026 Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic, with Joshua Stapleton and Petr Tichavský, posted a practical 48-multiplication algorithm in the same isotropy orbit that needs 204 other operations. These derived variants corroborate and extend the rank-48 bound. Journal publication of the Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic preprints is unconfirmed.

ai_role.statement: AlphaEvolve found the 48-multiplication scheme over the complex numbers. Researchers outside DeepMind then derived rational and faster variants from that decomposition by isotropies. A peer-reviewed ISSAC 2026 paper by Moran, Schwartz and Yuan recovers the rational form by a general method. These derivations depend on the AI result. They corroborate it without discovering the scheme independently. Kaporin had reported a 48-multiplication design with complex coefficients, found by numerical search, in 2024. AlphaEvolve was therefore not the first to reach a rank of 48 for 4x4 complex matrices.

evidence.citation: Moran, Y., Schwartz, O., Yuan, S., Complex to Rational Fast Matrix Multiplication, Proceedings of ISSAC 2026, pp. 297-304, 12 July 2026 (arXiv:2602.13171, 13 February 2026). The authors work at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and UC San Diego and have no tie to DeepMind; they treat AlphaEvolve's complex scheme as a valid algorithm, recover its rational equivalent by a general method, and prove that AlphaEvolve's schemes have no integer-coefficient equivalents.
evidence.title: Complex to Rational Fast Matrix Multiplication
evidence.quote: This method recovers the previously known ad hoc results of Dumas, Pernet, and Sedoglavic (2025) and extends them to more general settings

evidence.citation: Kaporin, I. E., Semi-analytical solution of Brent equations, Doklady Mathematics 110(1), published online 20 October 2024 (Russian edition: Doklady Rossijskoj akademii nauk 518(1), 2024). Kaporin works at the Federal Research Center Computer Science and Control of the Russian Academy of Sciences and has no tie to DeepMind; he reports that a numerical search found a (4,4,4;48) design, which challenges DeepMind's claim to be first.
evidence.title: Semi-analytical solution of Brent equations
evidence.quote: for the resulting fast matrix multiplication algorithms many known values of rank are reproduced and even improved, in particular, the designs (4,4,4;48) and (2,4,5;32) are found

evidence.citation: Li, X., Wang, Y., Hu, S., Substitution and quotient of the isotropy group action, arXiv:2607.15069, 16 July 2026 (version 2, 15 August 2026). The authors work at Zhejiang University of Technology and the National University of Defense Technology and have no tie to DeepMind; they parameterize the rational solution derived from AlphaEvolve's scheme and find infinitely many inequivalent rational 48-multiplication algorithms.
evidence.title: Substitution and quotient of the isotropy group action
evidence.quote: In the parameterized solution set, we can find infinitely many inequivalent 48-multiplication algorithms with only rational coefficients.

display.answer: DeepMind's blog post and technical paper come from the makers. The rational variants by Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic, by Moran, Schwartz and Yuan and by Li, Wang and Hu derive from AlphaEvolve's published decomposition. In separate work, Kaporin reached a 48-multiplication design in 2024 by numerical search.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: In May 2025 DeepMind reported that its Gemini-powered coding agent AlphaEvolve had found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices, a rank that Igor Kaporin had reported in 2024.
fields.account: In a Doklady Mathematics paper published online on 20 October 2024, Igor Kaporin of the Russian Academy of Sciences reported a 48-multiplication design for 4x4 matrices that he found by numerical search. On 14 May 2025 Google DeepMind announced AlphaEvolve, a Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent. DeepMind reported that it had found an algorithm multiplying two 4x4 complex-valued matrices with 48 scalar multiplications, improving on the 49 obtained from two recursion levels of Strassen's 1969 algorithm. The makers' technical paper, posted on 16 June 2025, states that AlphaEvolve is the first method to find a rank-48 algorithm for these matrices. The AlphaEvolve paper does not cite Kaporin's paper. On 16 June 2025 Jean-Guillaume Dumas, Clément Pernet and Alexandre Sedoglavic (CASC and CRIStAL, France), researchers independent of DeepMind, posted a preprint. It presents a 48-multiplication algorithm with only rational coefficients, removing the need for complex arithmetic. They state that it was derived from AlphaEvolve's algorithm under the action of an isotropy that projects the decomposition onto the field of rational numbers. The derivation is therefore not independent of the AI result. The first version of the preprint contains no explicit verification statement. On 19 March 2026 the same authors posted a more accurate variant of that rational algorithm, valid over any ring containing an inverse of 2. In a peer-reviewed ISSAC 2026 paper of 12 July 2026, Yoav Moran, Oded Schwartz and Shuncheng Yuan recover the rational form of AlphaEvolve's scheme by a general method and prove that the scheme has no integer-coefficient equivalent. On 16 July 2026 Li, Wang and Hu, of Zhejiang University of Technology and the National University of Defense Technology, posted a preprint in which they find infinitely many inequivalent rational 48-multiplication algorithms. Version 7 of the Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic preprint (27 July 2026) embeds a Maple program that checks their rational algorithm. On 10 September 2026 Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic, with Joshua Stapleton and Petr Tichavský, posted a practical 48-multiplication algorithm in the same isotropy orbit that needs 204 other operations. These derived variants corroborate and extend the rank-48 bound. Journal publication of the Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic preprints is unconfirmed.
